blocks.text: news

Seed Co Zambia Limited has continued to reaffirm its commitment to supporting education and community development through a donation of 606 sanitary packs to St. Michael Primary and Secondary School, an initiative aimed at ensuring the girl-child is uplifted.
The donation was received by Headteacher Mr Anthony Chilambwe, who shared the remarkable growth story of the school while welcoming the Seed Co team.

The Headteacher explained that the school has 1,024 learners, of which 534 are girls. The strong presence of girls at the school reflects the community’s growing commitment to promoting female education.

During the visit, Seed Co Zambia Managing Director Mrs Grace Tumeo Bwanali encouraged the girls to prioritise menstrual health and personal hygiene, explaining that access to proper sanitary products is essential for their health, confidence, and academic progress.

She noted that in many communities, girls are forced to use unsafe alternatives due to lack of resources, which can expose them to infections and discomfort. Access to safe sanitary towels, she emphasised, ensures that girls remain comfortable and able to participate fully in school life without missing lessons.

“When girls are supported with the right sanitary products and knowledge about menstrual hygiene, they remain in school, focus on their studies, and build the confidence needed to pursue their dreams.”

Beyond the immediate impact of the donation, the visit also carried a powerful message about the long-term value of educating girls. A girl who consistently attends school is more likely to complete her education, pursue professional careers, and contribute meaningfully to her community and nation. Mrs Bwanali was accompanied by senior members of the Seed Co management team being Tichaona Ravasingadi, Finance Director and Nyambe Mubita, Human Resources & Administration Manager.

In her vote of thanks, Head Girl Nalishebo Simbula expressed heartfelt gratitude to Seed Co Zambia for their generous gesture and extended her best wishes on behalf of St Michael’s School for Seed Co’s continued success in all its operations.

seedco-zambia-commemorates-world-environ.title: SeedCo Zambia Commemorates World Environment Day with Tree Planting and Clean-Up Activity

blocks.text: news

On Thursday, 11th June 2026, SeedCo Zambia joined the global community in commemorating World Environment Day, which is annually marked on 5th June, with a meaningful and hands-on celebration at our farm premises at SeedCo HQ in Lusaka.

Under this year’s theme, “Inspired by Nature, for Our Climate, and for Our Future,” staff members came together for a tree planting activity, and a litter pick around the company premises, planting a total of 200 trees on the day.

The commemoration was led by Managing Director, Mrs. Grace Tumeo Bwanali, who set the tone for the occasion. “The trees we are planting are more than just seedlings in the ground. They represent our commitment to protecting the environment,” she said.
Mrs. Bwanali challenged staff to reflect on their daily habits, from responsible plastic disposal and water conservation to energy usage at home.
She noted that plastic waste remains a serious environmental concern, taking decades or even centuries to decompose, and urged staff to consider the legacy their actions leave for future generations.

“If we do not take the initiative to clean up our environment, who will? We must lead by example,” she said. Safety, Health and Environmental Manager, Valentine Mutale, echoed the significance of the day for SeedCo as a business. “As a company operating in the seed industry, everything we do depends on natural resources, healthy ecosystems, and a stable climate,” he noted, reinforcing the company’s commitment to sustainability as central to its operations.

As part of its ongoing environmental stewardship, SeedCo Zambia continues to encourage staff to practise recycling and proper waste management through designated waste stations on site and off site. The events of yesterday reflect SeedCo Zambia’s belief that caring for the environment is not a once-a-year event, but a daily commitment, to our communities, our country, and the generations who will come after us.

Seeding Rates: The recommended average plant population for maize for grain in Zambia is currently at 50,000 plants per hectare. Our mission is to Breed, Seed and Feed Africa. Our main vision is to dominate the Seed Business in Africa through developing crop varieties i.e. maize hybrids, soya beans, wheat, sorghum, sugar beans, and cow peas, with stable performance across both environments and seasons. However, it is important to note that for Seed Co Limited the majority of these regional markets are developing countries which are the most vulnerable to climatic change effects due to limited resources to adapt. As such there is urgent need to give farmers hybrids that are adapted to climate change and give them the greatest yield. To achieve this, testing of crop varieties is carried out across different agro-ecologies (throughout Africa) to generate extensive genotype by environment interaction data.

Seed Co Limited also recognises the need to develop hybrids that fit specific environmental conditions. In addition, these varieties will also be coming from a background of an intense breeding programme whose focus is to select for abiotic (heat and drought, low nitrogen use efficiency, soil acidity and alkalinity), biotic (foliar and cob diseases) and response to different agronomic practices. Resultant effort has produced a number of crop varieties which have allowed farmers to easily adapt to the effects of climatic change in their farming systems and achieve highest yields possible.
